theory.intro: A **hemisphere** is half a sphere. The curved part is half of a sphere's surface, $\frac{1}{2} \times 4\pi r^{2} = 2\pi r^{2}$. Whether you add anything more depends on the solid: an **open** hemisphere (a hollow bowl or dome) has only the curved surface, while a **closed** hemisphere (a solid half-ball) also has a flat **circular face** of area $\pi r^{2}$.
facts: The curved surface of any hemisphere is $2\pi r^{2}$ — half of a sphere's $4\pi r^{2}$.
**Open** hemisphere (bowl, dome, half-pipe): $A = 2\pi r^{2}$ — the curved surface only, no flat face.
**Closed** hemisphere (solid half-ball): $A = 2\pi r^{2} + \pi r^{2} = 3\pi r^{2}$ — the curved surface plus the flat circular face.
Deciding **open or closed** is the whole skill: read whether the flat circle is a real surface of the object.
When a **diameter** is given, halve it to get $r$ before substituting.
Keep the working exact and round only on the last line; area is in **square** units.
steps: Decide whether the hemisphere is open or closed.
Write the matching formula: open $2\pi r^{2}$, closed $3\pi r^{2}$.
Substitute the radius, halving a diameter first, then evaluate.

development.question_text: A wooden dome ornament is a closed solid hemisphere of radius $9$ cm (its flat base is polished as well). Find its total surface area in exact form, in terms of $\pi$.
development.solution_text:
A closed hemisphere uses $3\pi r^{2}$.
$A = 3\pi r^{2}$
$= 3\pi(9)^{2}$
$= 243\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$

development.question_text: A hemispherical mixing bowl is open at the top (it has no flat face) and has a diameter of $24$ cm. Find the area of its curved surface, correct to $2$ decimal places.
A hemisphere has a radius of $5$ cm. Find its surface area in exact form in terms of $\pi$ if it is (a) open (no flat face) and (b) closed (including its flat face).
A half-orange is modelled as a closed hemisphere of radius $3.5$ cm (the flat cut face is included). Find its total surface area, correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
A closed hemisphere uses $3\pi r^{2}$.
$A = 3\pi r^{2}$
$= 3\pi(3.5)^{2}$
$= 36.75\pi$
$= 115.4535\ldots$
$\approx 115.45\text{ cm}^{2}$

development.question_text: An open hemispherical bowl has a curved surface area of $32\pi$ cm². Find its radius.
development.solution_text:
An open hemisphere uses $2\pi r^{2}$.
$2\pi r^{2} = 32\pi$
$r^{2} = 16$
$r = 4\text{ cm}$

development.question_text: A closed solid hemisphere has a total surface area of $108\pi$ m². Find its radius.
development.solution_text:
A closed hemisphere uses $3\pi r^{2}$.
$3\pi r^{2} = 108\pi$
$r^{2} = 36$
$r = 6\text{ m}$

mastery.question_text: A hemispherical dome roof has a radius of $8$ m. Only its curved outer surface is painted (the underside is open), at a cost of $\$5$ per square metre. Find the cost of the paint, correct to the nearest cent.
mastery.solution_text:
Only the curved surface is painted, so use $2\pi r^{2}$.
$A = 2\pi r^{2}$
$= 2\pi(8)^{2}$
$= 128\pi$
$= 402.1238\ldots\text{ m}^{2}$
Cost $= 5 \times 402.1238\ldots$
$= 2010.6192\ldots$
$\approx \$2010.62$

mastery.question_text: A closed solid hemisphere has a total surface area of $27\pi$ cm². Find its diameter.
mastery.solution_text:
A closed hemisphere uses $3\pi r^{2}$.
$3\pi r^{2} = 27\pi$
$r^{2} = 9$
$r = 3\text{ cm}$
$d = 2 \times 3 = 6\text{ cm}$

mastery.question_text: Two hemispheres each have a radius of $6$ cm. One is open (no flat face) and the other is closed (with its flat face). Find, in exact form in terms of $\pi$, how much greater the closed hemisphere's surface area is.
mastery.solution_text:
Closed: $3\pi r^{2}$
Open: $2\pi r^{2}$
Difference $= 3\pi r^{2} - 2\pi r^{2} = \pi r^{2}$
$= \pi(6)^{2}$
$= 36\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$

practice.coverageNote: Hemisphere surface area is a narrow atom whose variety is the open-vs-closed decision ($2\pi r^{2}$ vs $3\pi r^{2}$); cases cover open, closed, diameter-given, an open/closed contrast and reverse (area to radius) rather than extra number-swaps.
